decision: The guard is the existing assertVariableValue from src/core/object-handle.ts, called at the complete-path of every JobStore implementation. No new module is introduced for the guard: assertVariableValue is the single source of truth for variable-value classification (T-0015 FF-A4). Three deliverables: (1) JobStore.complete gains an optional third parameter payload?: Record<string,unknown>; each value is passed through assertVariableValue before state advance; a single ok:false returns {ok:false, code:'RECORD_IN_PAYLOAD'} fail-closed with job remaining LOCKED, all-or-nothing. (2) ci/checks/mutation-gateway-isolation.sh: structural isolation check asserting no writable accessor escapes the gateway boundary and assertVariableValue is called at the complete boundary. (3) ci/checks/flowable-bridge-contract.sh: deferred probe (FF-G3) that exits 0 when the bridge path is absent, activates when it exists. The fail path is not modified (carries no result payload). JSON-encoded strings are inert literals — guard does not parse string contents. T-0114 seam: after T-0114 merges, the guard is wired into both InMemoryJobStore and PostgresJobStore complete-paths identically — one function call, no duplication.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: assertVariableValue already exists in object-handle.ts and is the canonical single source of truth (FF-A4, T-0015). A wrapper module adds indirection without adding invariant. The BUILD contract is: call the existing function directly; the isolation check confirms the call site.

rejected_alternatives.option: Inline record-detection logic inside complete without importing object-handle.ts
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Would duplicate the record-detection logic, diverging from T-0015's canonical implementation. Two copies drift; one wins silently.

rejected_alternatives.option: Guard at enqueue time instead of complete time
rejected_alternatives.why_not: enqueue is producer-side; the threat is an external worker returning a result via complete. Guarding at enqueue does not protect against a malicious/buggy worker injecting a record via complete.

rejected_alternatives.option: Validate payload in a middleware/router layer above the store
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A record object could be constructed in application code and passed directly to complete without going through HTTP. The guard must be at the store boundary — the last defense before state mutation, testable at unit level.

rejected_alternatives.option: Parse JSON strings and check their decoded content inside assertVariableValue
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates the pure/total/side-effect-free contract; opens an unbounded attack surface; breaks the existing ok:true contract for string primitives already established by T-0015. Strings are inert literals, not objects.
fail carries no worker-supplied result payload today (only retries + retryTimeoutMs). No seam exists. Spec is explicit: the seam is complete.

contracts:
// src/core/types.ts — additive field on Job
export interface Job { readonly result?: Record<string, unknown>; /* + all existing fields unchanged */ }

// src/core/jobStore.ts — additive error code
export type ErrorCode = 'NOT_FOUND' | 'NOT_LOCKED' | 'LOCK_EXPIRED' | 'NOT_OWNER' | 'RECORD_IN_PAYLOAD';

// src/core/jobStore.ts — additive optional parameter
complete(workerId: string, jobId: string, payload?: Record<string, unknown>): CompleteResult;

// Guard algorithm: for each v in Object.values(payload ?? {}): r = assertVariableValue(v); if !r.ok return {ok:false, code:'RECORD_IN_PAYLOAD'} — job NOT advanced; then advance job to COMPLETED, store result = payload; return {ok:true}
// src/core/object-handle.ts NOT modified — assertVariableValue imported, not changed
// src/core/grant-resolver.ts NOT modified — resolveFor imported for bridge contract clause only
// T-0114 seam: BUILD must rebase on dev after T-0114 merges; wire assertVariableValue into complete-path of BOTH InMemoryJobStore and PostgresJobStore implementations

fitness_functions.rule: Structural isolation: no module outside src/core/grant-resolver.ts imports a symbol from a writable record accessor; no new *mutate*/*write*/*persist* function mapping a ResourceRef to record fields appears outside the gateway composition.

assertVariableValue call-site present at complete boundary: mutation-gateway-isolation.sh asserts assertVariableValue (or a thin wrapper calling it) is called in src/core/jobStore.ts complete method before advancing job state. Not optional, not flag-guarded.

Deferred Flowable bridge contract probe: exits 0 when no bridge path (src/bridge/ or src/core/flowable*.ts) exists. When bridge path IS present: asserts every bridge result-return file calls assertVariableValue; asserts record mutations route through resolveFor.

Complete payload fail-closed: JobStore.complete with payload containing a value where assertVariableValue returns ok:false returns {ok:false, code:'RECORD_IN_PAYLOAD'} and leaves the job in LOCKED state (not advanced). All-or-nothing: one invalid value in a payload of N values causes full rejection.
Clean payload and no-payload regression: complete with only handles + inert literals returns {ok:true} and advances to COMPLETED; complete without payload is byte-identical to existing behavior.

Additive — frozen exports unchanged: git diff for this task's commit does NOT touch src/core/object-handle.ts, src/core/grant-lattice.ts, or src/core/grant-resolver.ts. CompleteResult includes RECORD_IN_PAYLOAD alongside the existing four codes. tsc --noEmit passes.
No regression on pre-existing fitness functions: single-resolver.sh, no-record-in-variable.sh, object-handle-isolation.sh, grant-resolver-isolation.sh, audit_append_only.sh all remain green.
Write-op path is typed: any invocation of resolveFor with a write op compiles against the T-0018 Operation type with no cast; no ad-hoc string literal is accepted in a write-op position.
